notes: §1985:VIII.4.9.2 prints the relative WRITE as WRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ INVALID KEY ... ] [ NOT INVALID KEY ... ] [ END-WRITE ]. writeStatement parses it (no RECORD word: WRITE REL-REC RECORD is COBOL2269), SequentialIoBinder.BindWrite resolves record-name-1 and routes the relative file to KeyedIoBinder.BindWrite, which refuses ADVANCING (COBOL2269 through the phrase association) and END-OF-PAGE (COBOL1720) because the relative format prints no print-control phrase; at --std 85 the later additions are refused on recognition: FROM literal and FROM SPACES (VisitRecordFromPhrase, COBOL0871), FILE file-name (DeclinedFilePhrase, COBOL1706), RETRY (VisitRetryPhrase) and WITH NO LOCK (VisitRecordLockPhrase) COBOL0900, NOT INVALID KEY before INVALID KEY (VisitConditionalPhrases, COBOL0900). Probes at 85: (a) FROM a group into an OCCURS DEPENDING ON record (3 [4WXYZ]) and FROM a ref-modified WG-T(1:4) into the second record description run; (b) no record-name, FROM twice, a doubled INVALID KEY and a WORKING-STORAGE record-name are refused; (d) FROM a function-identifier (Amendment 1) runs; (e) dynamic, random and sequential access run (sequential numbers records 1, 2 and ignores the key), WRITE after CLOSE and WRITE on an INPUT-open file give status 48 with neither phrase executed; (f) duplicate key 22 and key 9999 behave. Relative key 0 reports 34 and skips INVALID KEY, a general-rule defect owned by kb/Work PB5125, not this format. The witness writes FROM with both phrases and END-WRITE in sequential access.

next.reason: 1985: "WRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ INVALID KEY imperative-statement-1 ] [ NOT INVALID KEY ...]"; 2023: "WRITE {record-name-1 | FILE file-name-1} [FROM {identifier-1 | literal-1}] [retry-phrase] [WITH [NO] LOCK] |INVALID KEY|". Format 2 adds FILE file-name-1, FROM literal-1, the retry phrase and the LOCK phrases. It also allows INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY in either order, so more programs are accepted.
